candidates.text: The conclusion that the use of the word try in the first sentence of the Impeachment Trial Clause lacks sufficient precision to afford any judicially manageable standard
candidates.speaker: Rehnquist
phrases: lacks sufficient precision to afford any judicially manageable standard
candidates.reason: States the holding's core rule: 'try' supplies no judicially manageable standard, fortified by the Clause's three express requirements.

candidates.text: But we conclude, after exercising that delicate responsibility, that the word try in the Impeachment Trial Clause does not provide an identifiable textual limit
candidates.speaker: Rehnquist
phrases: does not provide an identifiable textual limit on the authority
candidates.reason: The 'identifiable textual limits' line distinguishing Powell v. McCormack, central to the scholarship on when the doctrine applies.

candidates.text: Judicial involvement in impeachment proceedings, even if only for purposes of judicial review, is counterintuitive
candidates.speaker: Rehnquist
phrases: would eviscerate the important constitutional check
candidates.reason: The separation-of-powers rationale: courts should not police the check on themselves.

candidates.text: If the Senate were to act in a manner seriously threatening the integrity of its results
candidates.speaker: Souter
phrases: seriously threatening the integrity of its results
candidates.reason: The coin-toss reservation the Critique discusses.

candidates.text: Petitioner has not asked the Court to conduct his impeachment trial
candidates.speaker: White
candidates.reason: Leading separate opinion, but not the rule.
